authority.marking_model_note: ⚠️ CCEA marks by COMPETENCE LEVEL STRANDS, not by points. Each task is judged on THREE named strands at CL0–CL5, and the three-digit strand combination is then looked up in a published MARK GRID to give the mark range (e.g. Task 2 '332' = 11–12 of 21). Tasks 3 and 5 are the exception: they are marked with task-specific checklists and per-part descriptors, which is why their component marks below are real point tariffs. Our per-strand 'Worth' columns are a Sophicly presentation of the board's strands; the AUTHORITATIVE mark is always the grid mark. This delta is stated in the protocol header (PROTOCOL-STANDARD E2).

total.why: The mark scheme never prints a 150. The question paper does ('The total mark for this paper is 150. Section A (Writing) One task marked out of 87 marks. Section B (Reading) Four tasks marked out of 63 marks.' — ccea-lang-unit1-summer2025-paper.pdf p.1), and 87 + 21 + 12 + 20 + 10 = 150, which matches language-paper-specs.json ccea.language_u1.total.

LOCATOR. 'Tasks 3 and 5 will be assessed using task-specific checklists' — so this task is genuinely point-marked, in four parts: a reason and two pieces of supporting evidence from each of two paragraphs. 4 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 12.

components.label: 3(a) reason from paragraph one, in the student's own words
components.quote: Crediting each reason [up to a max. of 4 marks]
components.quote_note: Four best-fit descriptors: 4 'a clear and precise understanding … using his/her own words' · 3 'accurate understanding … mainly using his/her own words' · 2 'mostly accurate … but with reliance on the language of the text' · 1 'a general sense … relying heavily on the language of the text' · 0 no creditworthy response.

components.label: 3(b) two pieces of supporting evidence from paragraph one
components.quote: Crediting the supporting evidence [up to a max. of 2 marks
components.quote_note: '1 mark for each piece of supporting evidence'; 'Evidence may be reported or quoted'. The mark is the number of valid ticks (none, one or two).

components.label: 3(c) reason from paragraph two, in the student's own words
components.quote: Crediting each reason [up to a max. of 4 marks]
components.quote_note: Same descriptor ladder as 3(a); the mark scheme prints the instruction once and applies it to 3(a) and 3(c) ('Enter this mark in the scoring facility for 3(a) or 3(c)').

components.label: 3(d) two pieces of supporting evidence from paragraph two
components.quote: Crediting the supporting evidence [up to a max. of 2 marks
components.quote_note: Same as 3(b) ('the scoring facility for 3(b) or 3(d)'). The 2025 scheme also lists UNACCEPTABLE evidence for 3(d), so evidence is judged, not merely counted.

LOCATOR. Checklist-marked: two presentational features, each identified (1) and its intended effect explained (up to 4). 1 + 4 + 1 + 4 = 10.

components.quote_note: 'In each case the score awarded is zero or one mark'. The scheme prints a list of valid features (an aspect of colour, layout, background, font, the image of the characters, the image of the clock) and credits any other valid suggestion.

ao_warning.issue: language-paper-specs.json records this paper's AOs with AQA's numbering (AO5/AO6 for the writing task, AO1/AO2 for the reading tasks). CCEA's own mark scheme numbers them differently.
ao_warning.board_wording: 'Below are the relevant assessment objectives for English Language Unit 1. Reading AO3 Candidates must: (i) read and understand texts, selecting material appropriate to purpose; (ii) develop and sustain interpretations of writers' ideas and perspectives; and (iii) explain and evaluate how writers use linguistic, structural and presentational features to achieve effects and engage and influence the reader. Writing AO4 Candidates must: (i) write to communicate clearly, effectively and imaginatively…; (ii) organise information and ideas into structured and sequenced sentences, paragraphs and whole texts…; and (iii) use a range of sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar.'
